title: Estimated Prevalence and New Diagnoses of HIV and HIV among Injection Drug Users 2012 - Current County Annual Health
description:
This data set provides an estimate of the number of people living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Disease at the end of each year for 2012 through 2016 and the number of these persons who have injection drug use identified as the primary risk for having acquired the infection. The data sets also provides the number of new diagnoses of HIV Disease by county among all persons and among those with injection drug identified as the primary risk. These data are derived through HIV surveillance activities of the Pennsylvania Department of Health. Laboratories and providers are required to report HIV test results for all individuals with a result that indicates the presence of HIV infection. These include detectable viral load results and CD4 results below 200 cells.  These data are reported electronically to the Pennsylvania National Electronic Disease Surveillance System.  The most recent patient address information obtained from all reports (both HIV and non-HIV reports) is used to identify last known county of residence in 2016. Cases are also matched to lists that identify individuals who have been reported to be living outside of Pennsylvania by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to remove cases that are presumed to have moved from Pennsylvania. Address data for Philadelphia County cases are extracted from the Pennsylvania enhanced HIV/AIDS Reporting System.

IDU: use of non-prescribed injection drugs (e.g., heroin, fentanyl, cocaine, etc.)

HIV Disease: Confirmed infection with the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is a stage of  HIV Disease marked by a low CD4 count and/or certain co-morbid conditions.

description: What is Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by County? GDP is a comprehensive measure of the economies of counties. Gross domestic product estimates the value of the goods and services produced in an area. It can be used to compare the size and growth of county economies across the state. This dataset is not not adjusted for inflation and represents the value of the goods and services in dollars at the time of the estimate. If you are looking to evaluate the growth of county economies over time, use of the Real GDP which is adjusted for inflation would eliminate changes in GDP caused by increases or decreases in the value of the US dollar. More information about the BEA's GDP by County is available here: GDP by County, Metro and Other Areas. This product uses the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) Data API but is not endorsed or certified by BEA.

title: Industry Partnership Wage Program PY 2013-2017 Labor And Industry
description:
The data represents the percent change in wages for an individual who has wages recorded in the Unemployment Compensation (UC) wage record file in the quarter in which they completed Industry Partnership training and wages found in the UC wage record file for that individual four quarters later. The change could be an increase or a decrease in wages. For example, if an individual completed training in the third quarter of 2013 and earned $5,000 in that quarter and earned $7,500 in the third quarter of 2014 the percent change for that individual would be 50%. The file incudes a count of all individuals who benefited from industry partnership training, the workforce development area of the industry partnership, the training program completed and the percentage change in wages per individual training.  The top line of the file includes the overall percentage change for all trainings. 

*The goal for Labor & Industry is based on receiving $10 million to fund Industry Partnerships. 

This dataset is for Program Year 2013-2017 and will be updated annually due to federal release schedule.
There are many reasons why an individual’s wage may have changed dramatically. Some of the reasons for negative wage changes or large increases in wages are listed below (not an exhaustive list).
•	An individual may have left the job, was laid off, or retired within the year after they were trained.
•	An individual may have become ill and left work.
•	An individual may have accepted a job in or moved to another state.
•	An individual may have been working two jobs and switched to one, or vice versa. 
•	An individual’s hours may have been reduced/increased during a quarter. 
•	Overtime hours may have been reduced/increased during a quarter.
•	An individual may have taken family leave.
•	A bonus could have been paid right after training was completed.
•	Wage records may not have been reported.
•	An employer may have closed and laid off all of their employees.

description:

Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome, or neonatal drug withdrawal, is an array of problems that develops shortly after birth in newborns who were exposed to addictive drugs, most often opioids, while in the mother’s womb. Withdrawal signs develop because these newborns are no longer exposed to the drug for which they have become physically dependent. This analysis is restricted to newborns with Pennsylvania-state residence who were hospitalized in Pennsylvania hospitals.

title: Risky Prescribing Measures Quarter 3 2016 - Current Quarterly County & Statewide Health
description:
View quarterly trends in Risky Prescribing Measures, including: 
o	Number/Rate of Individuals Seeing 5+ Prescribers and 5+ Dispensers: Number of individuals who received prescriptions from 5 or more prescribers AND 5 or more dispensers for any Schedule II-V substance in a 3-month period. This measure is also referred to as Multiple Provider Episodes. County rates are calculated based on the patient’s county of residence. 
o	Number/Rate of Individuals Seeing 4+ Prescribers and 4+ Dispensers: Number of individuals who received prescriptions from 5 or more prescribers AND 5 or more dispensers for any Schedule II-V substance in a 3-month period. This measure is also referred to as Multiple Provider Episodes. County rates are calculated based on the patient’s county of residence. 
o	Number/Rate of Individuals Seeing 3+ Prescribers and 3+ Dispensers: Number of individuals who received prescriptions from 5 or more prescribers AND 5 or more dispensers for any Schedule II-V substance in a 3-month period. This measure is also referred to as Multiple Provider Episodes. County rates are calculated based on the patient’s county of residence. 
o	Number/Rate of Individuals with an Average Daily MME >50, >90 or >120: Average Daily MME is calculated as the sum of the total MME on each day in a time period based on all prescriptions an individual has filled divided by the number of days in the prescription(s).  Measures include the number and rate of individuals prescribed greater than 50 MME per day, greater than 90 MME per day, or greater than 120 MME per day and is based on the patient’s county of residence.
o	Number/Rate of Individuals with Overlapping Opioid/Benzodiazepine Prescriptions: Number of individuals receiving overlapping opioid and benzodiazepine prescriptions during a given quarter. This measure is based on the patients’ county of residence.
o	Number/Rate of Individuals with > 30 Days of Overlapping Opioid/Benzodiazepine Prescriptions: Number and rate of individuals receiving overlapping opioid and benzodiazepine prescriptions for 30 days or more during a given quarter using state/county populations as denominators. This measure is based on the patients’ county of residence. 
Please see PDMP Data Technical Notes for additional details: https://www.health.pa.gov/topics/programs/PDMP/Pages/Data.aspx

title: ESIF 2014-2020 categorisation ERDF-ESF-CF planned vs implemented
description:
This file contains categorisation data from the ERDF/ESF/Cohesion Fund programmes and in particular it  compares **PLANNED AMOUNTS TO IMPLEMENTED INVESTMENTS**. 
The data will be updated regularly to reflect updated information transmitted. 

***NEW*** 03/2020 - The Commission's COVID-19 response in 2020 involves encouraging reprogramming unallocated EU budget towards the COVID-19 health response and support to the economy, particularly through supporting SMEs and workers. Check out these data stories based on this dataset: 
-  HEALTH: https://cohesiondata.ec.europa.eu/stories/s/In-profile-cohesion-policy-improving-health-servic/qyuv-h9j2
-  SMEs: https://cohesiondata.ec.europa.eu/stories/s/An-Economy-that-works-for-people-Cohesion-Policy-s/n4ee-2h83

***NEW*** 12/2018 - CLIMATE AND BIODIVERSITY TRACKING: In December 2018 the calculation of amounts planned, decided and spend on categorisation codes (weighted 100% and 40%) for climate tracking and biodiversity tracking were added to the dataset to allow full transparency on how investment under these tracking systems are progressing. Specially designed charts providing visualisations on these tracking systems are linked to the dataset below.  

***NEW*** 12/2018 - OPERATIONS (projects) SELECTED: Also in December 2018 the number of operations (projects) linked to each categorisation value reported by priority axis is reflected in the dataset.  In many cases programmes provide detailed categorisation information, reporting more than one intervention field code for a specific operation. While leading to more detailed thematic information it leads to multiple reporting of some operations. 

TIMING AND FREQUENCY: The categorisation system implementation values are reported once a year by the 350+ programmes at end January. It is then published in this dataset towards the end of February. Thereafter the data is updated regularly to reflect the updated information transmitted by the programmes. 
This dataset currently contains data to end-2016 and end- 2017. As the data is cumulative the **ANNUAL VALUES SHOULD NOT BE AGGREGATED *** but may be compared to see progress. 

STRUCTURE OF DATASET: 
The planned data is provided in tables one for each priority axis (investment pillar) of each programme. The categorisation systems is defined in Implementing Regulation 215/2014 with 8 dimensions in total - http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32014R0215.
These dimension represent different ways of categorising the nature of the EU support (i.e. the intervention (activity) field, the form of finance, the territorial context, etc.).
In the programme documents only four4 dimensions were encoded for ERDF/ Cohesion Fund while five5 dimensions were encoded for ESF and can be found in the dataset. Data on three3 other dimensions is only provided in the implementation reports - Location, Economic Dimension, ERDF/CF Thematic Objective - and therefore there is no planned amount to compare. 
In analysing the content of the dataset **THE DIFFERENT DIMENSIONS SHOULD BE ANALYSED SEPARATELY AS OTHERWISE DOUBLE COUNTING OF FINANCIAL AMOUNTS WILL OCCUR**. 
This information note provides more detail on the categorisation system 2014-2020: http://ec.europa.eu/regional_policy/sources/docgener/informat/2014/guidance_categorisation_climate_en.pdf

ANALYSING THEMATIC CONTENT AND PROGRESS: A second dataset found here - https://cohesiondata.ec.europa.eu/EU-Level/ESIF-2014-2020-Categorisation-Crosscutting-Themes-/xns4-t7ym - provides a lookup table for understanding how the Commission uses the intervention field codes to look at cross cutting issues such as investments in "innovation", "enterprise support", etc. That "lookup" dataset also has the "climate change tracking" and "biodiversity tracking" weightings.

title: A METHODOLOGICAL SYSTEM FOR PROFESSIONALLY ORIENTED PHYSICS TEACHING IN CHEMICAL TECHNOLOGY PROGRAMS: DESIGN AND EXPERIMENTAL VERIFICATION
description: This article reports a study on the scientific and methodological basis of professionally oriented physics teaching for students of chemical engineering and technology at universities. The topic is relevant because industry, driven by digital transformation, Industry 4.0, intelligent manufacturing and the shift to a knowledge-based economy, now expects a new kind of engineer. Our analysis shows that the traditional physics course, built mainly around fundamental laws and standard problems, does not give students enough practice in applying physical principles to the analysis and design of technological processes. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23274702
tags: ["professionally oriented physics education; engineering education; chemical engineering and technology education; chemical process engineering; methodological system; competency-based approach; digital educational environment; virtual laboratory; artificial intelligence."]

title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF PROVERBS IN ENGLISH AND UZBEK: LINGUOCULTURAL AND SEMANTIC PERSPECTIVES
description: This article compares English and Uzbek proverbs from semantic and linguocultural perspectives. It shows that many proverbs in the two languages express the same universal ideas about work, knowledge, friendship, patience and caution, but encode them through different images rooted in each nation's history, economy, religion and daily life. The study classifies proverb pairs into full, partial and zero equivalents and identifies culture-specific values: the central role of family, elders, hospitality and community in Uzbek proverbs, and of individual responsibility, time and pragmatism in English ones. Structural and stylistic features such as rhyme, parallelism and ellipsis are also compared. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23238699
tags: ["proverb, paremiology, linguoculture, national worldview, equivalence, semantics, English, Uzbek."]

title: CONTEMPORARY TRANSFORMATION OF THE PRODUCT LIFE CYCLE (IN TEXTILE PRODUCTS)
description: This article examines how digitalization, fast and ultra-fast fashion, and circular-economy regulation are reshaping the conventional product life cycle (PLC) in the textile and apparel industry. The study combines conceptual synthesis with secondary-data analysis from academic literature, the European Environment Agency, the European Commission, the Ellen MacArthur Foundation, McKinsey & Company, and the National Statistics Committee of Uzbekistan. The analysis distinguishes between the commercial life of a fashion item, which is becoming shorter and more data-driven, and the material life of textile products, which policy and circular business models seek to extend through durability, reuse, repair, resale, and fibre-to-fibre recycling. Evidence from Europe and Uzbekistan is used to show that competitive PLC management increasingly depends on rapid market sensing, flexible production, demand forecasting, circular design, and traceability. The paper proposes a dual-loop PLC framework and practical priorities for Uzbek textile enterprises seeking to move from cost-based competition toward higher-value, responsive, and sustainable export models. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23236893
tags: ["Product Life Cycle (PLC), textile industry, fast fashion, ultra-fast fashion, circular economy, digitalization, PLM, sustainability, Uzbekistan."]

title: Circular Economy Business Case Calculator
description: The Circular Economy Business Case Calculator is an Excel-based tool designed to assist companies in the economic evaluation of circular economy business models (CBMs). It enables a structured and transparent assessment of financial viability by modelling revenue streams, capital and operating expenditures (CapEX, OpEx) as well as financing costs in detail. The tool provides a clear and visually intuitive graphical representation of the results as an output. The current version (v1.2) of the calculator, developed by the Wuppertal Institute as part of the R-evolve project, covers the following CBMs, including several sub-strategies: Repair, Reuse, Refurbish, Remanufacture, Repurpose, Recycle and Rethink (in the form of Rental). It also enables the parallel calculation and comparison of several scenarios, such as different sales markets or forecasts. Further features and business models will be included in future updates.  This tool has been carefully developed and tested. However, minor errors cannot be entirely ruled out. Please note that we accept no liability for any misrepresentations or miscalculations, nor for decisions made on the basis of the results. We welcome your feedback to help us further improve and refine the calculator (see Contact). DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23242078

title: Code, data and outputs for: Green hydrogen from floating photovoltaics on UK reservoirs
description: Code, input data, model outputs and figures supporting the article “Green hydrogen from floating photovoltaics on UK reservoirs: hourly techno-economic, water and ecological assessment under uncertainty” (Al Talai, Al-Mandhari, Hussain and Ghosh; manuscript under review). The Python model simulates hourly floating photovoltaic (FPV) generation and PEM electrolysis at twelve UK reservoirs over 2005 to 2023, with size-dependent costs, hydrogen storage, a reservoir energy balance and uncertainty analysis (Monte Carlo, Sobol indices, scenario discovery). The package contains: all model and figure scripts (code/); the results behind every table and figure (results/); the article and supplementary figures (figures/); a parameter register with sources; PVsyst files for the cross-verification; a GeoPackage of UK waterbodies, boundaries and Ramsar sites used for site selection and Fig. 2. README.md explains how to reproduce every result. Hourly PVGIS weather is public and is downloaded by the code. Third-party data keep their original terms: the UKCEH Spatial inventory of UK waterbodies (doi:10.5285/b6b92ce3-dcd7-4f0b-8e43-e937ddf1d4eb), and the ONS boundaries and JNCC Ramsar sites, all under the Open Government Licence v3.0. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23297220
tags: ["floating photovoltaics; green hydrogen; PEM electrolysis; electrolyser sizing; techno-economic analysis; levelised cost of hydrogen; reservoir evaporation; uncertainty quantification; pvlib; United Kingdom"]

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND THE COMPETITIVENESS OF SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES IN UZBEKISTAN: CHALLENGES, OPPORTUNITIES AND STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
description: Digital transformation has become one of the most important drivers of economic growth, business competitiveness and structural modernization in developing economies. In Uzbekistan, the rapid expansion of digital infrastructure, electronic government services, financial technologies, e-commerce and innovative business models has created new opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). At the same time, insufficient digital skills, limited financial resources, technological disparities and inadequate managerial competencies continue to constrain the effective adoption of digital technologies by businesses. This article examines the role of digital transformation in increasing the competitiveness of SMEs in Uzbekistan. The study analyzes the main economic benefits of digitalization, identifies existing barriers to technology adoption, and proposes strategic priorities for improving the digital competitiveness of enterprises. Particular attention is paid to digital skills, access to finance, e-commerce, artificial intelligence, data-driven management and institutional support. The study concludes that the competitiveness of SMEs can be significantly strengthened through an integrated policy combining digital infrastructure development, human capital formation, financial incentives and modern business management practices. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23220056

title: DIGITALIZATION OF PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP PROJECT ASSESSMENT AND CONCEPT DEVELOPMENT THROUGH AN ELECTRONIC PLATFORM: THE CASE OF WATER MANAGEMENT
description: The digitalization of Public-Private Partnership project assessment is becoming an increasingly important mechanism for improving the transparency, efficiency, and quality of infrastructure investment decisions, particularly in the water management sector where projects involve substantial capital requirements, long implementation periods, complex technical systems, environmental considerations, and significant operational risks. This article develops an integrated electronic-platform framework for the identification, screening, assessment, financial and economic evaluation, risk allocation, concept development, procurement preparation, and subsequent monitoring of Public-Private Partnership projects in water management, with particular attention to its potential application in Uzbekistan. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23232301
tags: ["Digitalization, partnership, infrastructure, water, assessment, investment, finance, risk, platform, governance."]

title: DYNAMICS OF KARAKUL PRODUCTION VOLUME AND TRADE INDICATORS
description: This article examines the historical dynamics of Karakul production and trade indicators in Uzbekistan. It focuses on the procurement of Karakul skins, state purchases, domestic and foreign trade, and factors affecting production volumes. Statistical evidence is used to identify the main stages of industry development, regional characteristics, and economic significance. The study aims to assess the role of Karakul sheep breeding in Uzbekistan’s agricultural and export systems. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23220160

title: Data and Online Appendix for: From a reflexively defensive philosophy to a proactively managerial philosophy: An empirical test of intellectual property management capability and artificial intelligence awareness among creators in Vietnam's cultural industries
description: Data and Online Appendix (S1 to S15) for a survey of 478 creators in Vietnam's cultural industries (January to July 2026), analysed by partial least squares structural equation modelling. The PDF contains the measurement instrument, the detailed results of the analyses reported in the article, the codebook and the anonymised dataset of the model. Three files are attached inside the PDF (Attachments panel): the dataset as a CSV file, the SmartPLS 3 project of the main and alternative models, and the Python and R scripts of the Gaussian copula analysis. The model relates the performance that creators attribute to intellectual property protection (INO, measured by INO2, INO3 and INO5) to intellectual property management capability (IPM), awareness of artificial intelligence in relation to copyright (AI_IPR), engagement with enforcement (IPEa), perceived accessibility of enforcement (IPEb) and perceived institutional quality (INS). Other questionnaire items, including free-text answers, are not included, to protect respondent confidentiality. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23236643

title: Data for "Future biodiversity risks of construction aggregate mining"
description: This dataset contains model outputs and figure source data for a global assessment of construction-aggregate extraction, mining-area expansion and biodiversity exposure. global extraction.zip contains annual sand, gravel and limestone extraction for 142 economies from 2023 to 2050 under business-as-usual (BAU) and circular-economy (CE) scenarios. Each economy has three material worksheets containing 10,000 Monte Carlo results per year, expressed in kilotonnes. mining area.zip contains cumulative additional mining area over 2023–2050, in km² per grid cell at 50-km resolution. It covers BAU, CE, conservation-oriented planning (CON), and an integrated action portfolio combining CE and CON (IAP), with 27 demand–reserve–area parameter combinations per scenario. mining-biodiversity overlap.zip contains the corresponding 50-km biodiversity exposure rasters for the same scenarios and parameter combinations, expressed in species-range equivalents per grid cell. rarity-weighted richness.zip contains 25 biodiversity rasters at 50-km resolution for mammals, birds, amphibians, reptiles and their combined total, including overall and threat-category layers. figure data.zip contains eight GeoTIFFs supporting Figures 1b, 1e, 2d, 2f, 3d and Extended Data Figures 2a and 3. Extended Data Figure 3 provides global mining suitability at 1-km resolution; divide the stored values by 10,000 to obtain suitability scores on a 0–1 scale. Analysis code is available in the aggregate-mining-biodiversity repository . DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23290764

title: ECONOMETRIC ASSESSMENT OF THE IMPACT OF PRODUCTION FACTORS ON IMPROVING THE ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY OF FOOD INDUSTRY ENTERPRISES
description: Abstract: In the context of increasing market competition, fluctuating input prices, and growing demand for high-quality food products, identifying the influence of these factors on enterprise performance has become an important research priority. This article examines the application of econometric methods to assess the impact of production factors on improving the economic efficiency of food industry enterprises. Particular attention is given to the relationships between labor productivity, capital investment, material costs, energy consumption, production capacity utilization, and financial performance. Correlation and regression analysis are considered as methodological instruments for identifying the statistical relationships between production inputs and economic outcomes. The study also discusses the importance of model specification, statistical diagnostics, and reliable data in obtaining valid econometric estimates. The proposed methodological approach can support the identification of major efficiency determinants, the optimization of production resources, the reduction of operating costs, and the improvement of managerial decision-making. The research provides a theoretical and methodological basis for further empirical studies aimed at strengthening the competitiveness and sustainable development of food industry enterprises. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23286653

title: EMPLOYEE MOTIVATION AND HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT AS KEY DRIVERS OF SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH
description: Employee motivation and human resource development are essential factors that influencing organizational performance, economic growth, and long-term business sustainability. In an increasingly competitive business environment, organizations should develop effective strategies to improve employee productivity, strengthen workforce capabilities, and promote sustainable management practices. The article gives information about the relationship between employee motivation, leadership effectiveness, training and development, and sustainable economic growth through a review of seven academic studies published between 2019 and 2025. The study shows a qualitative literature review approach to synthesize findings from research conducted in different organizational and geographical contexts, including Indonesia, Ukraine, Cambodia, and Nigeria. The reviewed literature indicates that employee motivation contributes to organizational sustainability by encouraging workforce engagement, enhancing productivity, supporting innovation, and improving organizational adaptability. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23295140
tags: ["Employee motivation, human resource management, sustainable development, employee productivity, leadership, training and development, organizational performance, economic growth."]

title: Egypt Census Village Deprivation Dataset
description: This dataset contains village-level deprivation indicators derived from Egypt's 2017 Population and Housing Census. It covers 4,702 rural villages across 24 governorates in Egypt and represents the complete rural settlement system included in the study, rather than a sample. The dataset was developed to examine multidimensional deprivation patterns and identify potential deprivation traps in Egypt's rural settlement system. It includes nine binary deprivation indicators covering housing conditions, infrastructure, education, gender and livelihoods. These indicators are used in an energy landscape analysis based on a pairwise maximum-entropy model to identify stable deprivation states, barriers between states and potential policy leverage points. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23269874

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF DIGITAL MANAGEMENT TECHNOLOGIES AND ASSESSMENT OF THEIR EFFECTIVENESS IN SERVICE ENTERPRISES
description: Abstract. This article discusses the digitalization of not only internal management systems in service enterprises, but also the development of the service sector. The features, trends and ways of further development of management services, the current state and global trends of the digital economy were analyzed, and measures for its further development in Uzbekistan were proposed. The article also reviewed research on innovative infrastructure facilities for managing innovative ecosystem services. Also, proposals and recommendations for the digitalization of the service sector were developed. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23245819

title: IMPROVING CUSTOMER-CENTRIC MANAGEMENT IN COMMERCIAL BANKS
description: This paper develops scientific and methodological foundations and practical recommendations for improving customer-centric management in commercial banks. Economic and statistical analysis, comparative analysis, a systems approach and expert assessment were used. The findings substantiate the need for deeper customer segmentation, service personalization and new service models based on digital technologies and artificial intelligence. Recommendations address the effectiveness of customer relationship management (CRM) systems, continuous staff development and a customer-centric corporate culture. The proposed measures serve to strengthen customer loyalty, improve service quality and expand banks' market share. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23275323

title: INSTITUTIONAL AND LEGAL FOUNDATIONS OF THE FORMATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE VALUE ADDED TAX SYSTEM IN THE REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN
description: This article examines the formation and development of the value added tax (VAT) system in Uzbekistan from the early transition years to the present. Using doctrinal legal analysis, historical-comparative and institutional approaches, it traces how the legal framework moved from fragmented regulation to a codified system and identifies the institutional drivers of reform. The study finds that the evolution of VAT in Uzbekistan has followed three directions: codification and unification of rules, gradual rate and base rationalization, and digitalization of administration. It also identifies persisting challenges, including refund delays, tax gaps, and the frequency of legislative change. The article concludes with policy recommendations for strengthening legal certainty and administrative efficiency. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23232448
tags: ["value added tax, Uzbekistan, Tax Code, tax reform, institutional framework, tax administration, digital economy"]

title: METHODS FOR DETERMINING IONIZING RADIATION DOSE RATE AND ITS HYGIENIC ASSESSMENT
description: Ionizing radiation sources are widely used in medicine, industry, scientific research, and other fields. However, the biological effects of ionizing radiation depend on its type, energy, absorbed dose, dose rate, and duration of exposure. Therefore, proper dosimetric monitoring and accurate determination of dose rate are important components of radiation safety. This article describes the concept of ionizing radiation dose rate, the main dosimetric methods used for its determination, the instruments applied for measurements, and the basic principles for hygienic assessment of the obtained results. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23239097

title: METHODS FOR ESTIMATING THE ASYMPTOTIC COMPLEXITY OF ALGORITHMS AND ANALYSIS OF THEIR EFFICIENCY INDICATORS
description: This article examines the theoretical and practical aspects of evaluating the efficiency and resource economy of algorithms in software development. In an era of rapid growth of information technology and big data, the processing speed of software systems and the rational use of memory resources have become a matter of priority. Within the scope of the study, the content of the asymptotic analysis apparatus used to determine the time and space complexity of algorithms, namely the mathematical notations Big O, Big Omega, and Big Theta, is covered extensively. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23243536

title: Metagenomic and transcriptomic analyses of tomato rhizosphere and leaves treated with a biowaste-derived extract
description: PERCIVAL (Processi di EstRazione di bioprodotti da sCarti agroIndustriali e VALorizzazione in cascata) project (PON  ARS01_00869) focuses on the development and optimization of innovative processes for the valorization of agro-industrial residues using a cascade biorefinery approach. The project aims to maximize resource efficiency by enabling the sequential recovery of high-value products from heterogeneous biomass streams. The targeted outputs include bioactive compounds (e.g. antioxidants and polyphenols), chemical building blocks (e.g. lactic acid), and advanced materials (e.g. nutraceutical ingredients, high-performance fibers, and bioplastics such as PLA). Residual fractions generated along the processing chain are further exploited for the production of biofuels (e.g. biomethane) and agricultural inputs (e.g. soil amendments, biochar, and biostimulants). Biological and molecular data generated within the project support the characterization, screening, and optimization of bioprocesses and feedstocks. The project also includes the assessment of environmental and economic sustainability of the proposed value chains, considering the entire lifecycle from raw material sourcing to final product generation. The data provided in this repository relate to a controlled-condition experiment on pot-grown tomato plants ( Solanum lycopersicum cv. Moneymaker). Plants were treated weekly with two different doses of a biowaste-based extract. To assess the efficacy and impact of this treatment, a multi-disciplinary approach was applied, encompassing:  Rhizosphere eDNA metabarcoding (16S and ITS)  Plant transcriptomics (RNA-Seq)  Plant physiological phenotyping  Soil and leaf chemical analyses The raw omics sequencing reads associated with this study have been deposited at the NCBI Sequence Read Archive (SRA) under BioProject PRJNA1425279. Data file inventory and description: SRA Sample description.csv : BioSample accession, experimental group, internal sample ID and SRA run identifier of each of the 184 sequencing libraries (RNA-seq and metabarcoding). RNAseq preprocessing.csv : number of read pairs per library along the RNA-seq pipeline (raw, after fastp pre-processing, uniquely mapped by STAR, assigned to genes by featureCounts) for the 60 libraries; data shown in Figure 2a. RNAseq quality.csv : sequencing statistics of the 60 RNA-seq libraries: library, flowcell and lane, raw reads, raw data (Gbp), base-call error rate, Q20 and Q30 percentages and GC content. RNAseq_rawcounts.tsv : raw gene-level read counts (featureCounts) of the annotated tomato genes (ITAG5.0) in the 60 leaf libraries. RNAseq_CPM.tsv : expression levels of the same genes and libraries, normalized as counts per million (CPM). eDNA seq preprocessing.csv : per-library read counts of the 124 amplicon libraries along the pre-processing and clustering pipeline: raw reads, reads after pre-processing, number of ASVs and number of singletons. Taxa table.xlsx : Excel workbook of four sheets with the complete taxonomic assignments and the absolute abundance tables (read counts) of the rhizosphere eDNA metabarcoding, for the 16S (bacterial) and ITS (fungal) communities. Physiological_parameters_v2.xlsx : biometric and ecophysiological measurements of each plant at 3 and 6 weeks (growth parameters, Dualex epidermal flavonol, anthocyanin and chlorophyll indices, fresh and air-dry weight) and its phenological stage on the BBCH scale. Soil chemical analysis_v2.xlsx : physicochemical properties of the pot soil at the end of each experiment (pH, total N, organic carbon fractions, exchangeable K and Mg, cation exchange capacity, Olsen P) and the ICP-OES instrument configuration and operating parameters. Tomato leaves chemical analysis_v1.xlsx : macronutrient content (N, P, Ca, Mg, K) of 30 leaf samples, with the analytical methods. Greenhouse climatic conditions.xlsx : hourly temperature, relative humidity and light intensity recorded over the 42 days of eac

title: Replication package for "AI, Structural Power and Governance Fragmentation: A Systematic Review and the Geopolitical AI Power Framework"
description: Replication package for a PRISMA 2020 systematic review on artificial intelligence and structural power in the global political economy. It contains the exact Scopus and Web of Science queries (5 October 2026) and record counts per stage; the screening decisions for 1,199 deduplicated records, including a rule-based screener, a zero-shot natural language inference screener (BART-large-MNLI) and the adjudication of conflicts; keyword co-occurrence data and Louvain clusters for the 330 included studies; the 49-study qualitative core; the Python scripts used for screening, mapping and reference verification; and the article's figures. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23248084

title: Supplementary Information: Techno-economic and environmental investigation of Power-to-X at various greenfield and brownfield levels - a structured multi-level infrastructure access framework for PtX
description: Description: This dataset contains the complete input parameters, life cycle inventory (LCI) data, and simulation results underlying the techno-economic and life cycle assessment (LCA) presented in "Techno-economic and environmental investigation of Power-to-X at various greenfield and brownfield levels - a structured multi-level infrastructure access framework for PtX". The study evaluates Power-to-X (PtX) pathways for producing hydrogen-derived products (e.g., ammonia, methanol, Fischer-Tropsch fuels, synthetic methane) from renewable electricity via PEM electrolysis, including energy system optimization (oemof) and cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment across multiple scenarios. The workbook is organized into the following sheets: Techno-economic input parameters Oemof_data — Technology-specific techno-economic parameters (CAPEX, OPEX, efficiencies, lifetimes, WACC) for all components of the energy system model (PV, wind onshore, battery storage, CO₂ capture (MEA), DAC, cryogenic ASU, PEM electrolysis, H₂ pressure storage, heat pump, heat storage, Haber-Bosch, methanol synthesis), with data sources and comments for each value. WACC — Weighted average cost of capital assumptions used in the annuity calculations. LCA_assumptions_H2 purchase — Assumptions for scenarios involving purchased (rather than on-site produced) hydrogen. Life cycle inventories (LCI) LCI_Electricity mix, LCI_Battery, LCI_PEM, LCI_H2 Storage, LCI_HP, LCI_Heat Storage, LCI_ASU, LCI_DAC, LCI_MEA, LCI_Methanation, LCI_Methanol, LCI_FT, LCI_HB — Process-specific life cycle inventories (material and energy flows per functional unit) for each technology, compiled from literature and/or ecoinvent-based sources, used as input to the LCA model. Results Results_LCA — Life cycle impact assessment results (e.g., climate change impact and other categories) disaggregated by technology, parameter, and scenario, across all modeled scenarios (e.g., greenfield/brownfield configurations for ammonia, methanol, and Fischer-Tropsch production). Results_oemof — Energy system optimization results (installed capacities, energy flows, investment and operational costs) per scenario, as produced by the oemof energy system model. Sensitivities — Results of the sensitivity cases of Sections 3.4.1 and 3.4.2: isolated infrastructure options compared with the cumulative chain (methanol, Germany) and the time-of-use electricity price case (ammonia, South Africa, Level 2), each with oemof and LCA results. Time_Series_electricity_price — Hourly time-of-use electricity price series for South Africa (8,760 h) derived from the Eskom Megaflex tariff, in R-cent/kWh and €-ct/kWh, with date, weekday, season and TOU period. CO2_price_parity — Calculation of the carbon price at which the LCOP of each product (Level 5) reaches parity with its fossil benchmark: GWP of the PtX products, fossil production and combustion emission factors, LCOP and resulting parity prices for Chile and Germany. Retrofit Costs — Indicative retrofit cost case for Level 5 (10% of the new-build CAPEX of the synthesis unit): LCOP of Level 5 with and without retrofit and the resulting Level 5 benefit for all products and locations. Tornado_parameter — Parameters varied in the tornado analysis (CAPEX of PEM electrolysis and wind turbines, electricity price, hydrogen price, WACC) with base values, lower and upper bounds and the basis for each bound. Tornado_results — Results of all one-at-a-time parameter variations (methanol, Levels 1–4, all three locations; 96 optimization runs) as the basis for Figure 9 and Table 5 of the manuscript. Context / related publication: This dataset accompanies the manuscript "Techno-economic and environmental investigation of Power-to-X at various greenfield and brownfield levels - a structured multi-level infrastructure access framework for PtX" by Heberl, Geiss, Rank, Hofrichter, Tran and Sterner. title: THE ESTABLISHMENT OF MULTIPLE FORMS OF OWNERSHIP IN AGRICULTURE AND THE CHANGE IN THE PEASANT'S ATTITUDE TO LAND
description: The article analyses the agrarian reforms carried out in Uzbekistan, particularly in the Kashkadarya and Surkhandarya regions, from the late 1980s to the 2010s. It examines the allocation of household plots to the rural population, the transformation of state farms into other forms of ownership, the establishment of shirkat (cooperative) and dehkan farms and the introduction of leasing, as well as the impact of these processes on the peasant’s attitude to land and property. The problems that arose in the course of the reforms and their causes are also shown. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23215051

title: THE EVOLUTION OF ECONOMIC THOUGHT ON SERVICES AND VALUE CREATION
description: This article reviews how economic thought, from classical political economy to modern service research, has understood the role of services in creating wealth and value. The approaches are compared by what they count as productive activity, what they analyze (a sector, a firm, or a market), and how they explain value creation through services. Five positions are identified: early views linking productive activity to agriculture or material accumulation; Marx’s concept of surplus value; the neoclassical view based on utility and market exchange; theories of structural change and the knowledge economy; and modern approaches in which value is created through service provision, use, and interaction. These positions overlap rather than form stages that every economy must pass through, and the article also separates the growth of the service sector from the servitization of firms and from service-dominant logic. It concludes that modern approaches widen the study of services without removing sectoral differences or the importance of material production, while the proposed matrix helps compare theories with different meanings of value and productivity. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23239734

title: TIMBER: A Trade-Instruction Multimodal Benchmark for Evidence Retrieval in German-Language Video Question Answering
description: TIMBER is a German-language multimodal video question answering benchmark for the skilled trades, built from publicly available instructional videos on YouTube. It comprises 155 videos (~27 hours) across 15 activity fields, with 310 question–answer pairs phrased in the register of an apprentice, each grounded in its source video by a temporal evidence span. Each question carries three labels: question type, required modality, and knowledge accessibility (explicit / derivable / implicit), the analytical core of the benchmark. The corpus additionally carries a manually produced segment-level annotation layer of 1,300 action segments with objects and on-screen text as oriented bounding boxes. Copyright note: This record contains only annotations and pointers (video IDs and timestamps) to the public source videos. No video, audio, frames, or transcripts are redistributed. The CC BY 4.0 licence covers only the annotations and codebook. The source videos remain subject to YouTube's terms and their creators' rights. Contents: timber_qa_catalog.csv - 310 QA pairs with labels and evidence spans, and the external answer source for implicit items timber_video_metadata.csv - metadata for all 155 videos timber_annotations.zip - 155 segment-level annotation files (JSON) codebook.md, README.md, LICENSE.txt The benchmark is intended for evaluation rather than training. It is described in the paper "TIMBER: A Trade-Instruction Multimodal Benchmark for Evidence Retrieval in German-Language Video Question Answering", KEEPER 2026 Workshop, co-located with ACM CIKM 2026, Rome, Italy (CEUR Workshop Proceedings, to appear). Funding: This work was conducted as part of the project "KINO Handwerk – Künstliche Intelligenz Niederbayern-Oberpfalz im Handwerk", funded by the Bavarian State Ministry of Economic Affairs, Regional Development and Energy (StMWi) under grant no. 20-3246.1-5-3. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23235122

title: USING CIRCULAR ECONOMY STRATEGIES TO ENHANCE COMPANY COMPETITIVENESS
description: The article analyzes the application of circular economy strategies as a primary mechanism for maintaining and enhancing company competitiveness in modern markets. Moving away from the traditional "take-make-dispose" linear model, four core circular strategies are examined: resource recovery, product life extension, sharing platforms, and product-as-a-service models. The study evaluates how these models directly influence competitive advantage through cost reduction, innovation, regulatory resilience, and enhanced brand equity. The article concludes with an assessment of how transition economies can implement these strategies and provides practical recommendations for corporate leaders seeking long-term sustainability. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23236072
tags: ["circular economy, company competitiveness, sustainable development, resource efficiency, product life cycle, innovation strategies, cost reduction."]
